Who to watch

Yale leaders (2026, through their last game)

  • Passing: #2 Dante Reno — 130/222, 1527 yds, 17 TD, 6 INT
  • Rushing: #6 Hugo Djeumeni Kemeni — 163 car, 921 yds, 6 TD
  • Receiving: #18 Jaxton Santiago — 45 rec, 638 yds, 8 TD
  • Tackles: #8 Phoenix Grant — 55
  • Sacks: #1 Zairion Jackson-Bass — 2.5

Yale won the Ivy League last year and has beaten Brown eight straight times. This year's Bulldogs are 4-3, 2-2 in the league, after a 26-8 win at Columbia. Quarterback Dante Reno has 17 touchdown passes, freshman Hugo Djeumeni Kemeni has run for 921 yards, and Jaxton Santiago has 8 touchdown catches. Yale coach Kevin Cahill on Brown: "playing with confidence and tremendous momentum" (Yale Athletics, Nov. 5, as indexed; ESPN).

Brown leaders (2026, through their last game)

  • Passing: #15 James Murphy — 160/255, 1792 yds, 4 TD, 10 INT
  • Rushing: #2 Matt Childs — 106 car, 426 yds, 7 TD
  • Receiving: #2 Matt Childs — 40 rec, 447 yds, 1 TD
  • Tackles: #10 Max Malo — 78
  • Sacks: #0 Ike Odimegwu — 4.5

Brown has won two straight: 38-31 in overtime over Cornell, then 36-17 over Penn on Oct. 31, when Drew Crabtree made three field goals and linebacker Max Malo returned a kickoff 45 yards for a touchdown. The defense allows about 16 points a game. Yale has won the last eight meetings (ESPN; Yale Athletics' preview, as indexed).

The series: Yale vs. Brown

All-time: Yale leads 89-35-5 in 129 meetings since 1880, and has beaten Brown more than any other opponent. Yale has won eight straight and is 50-23-1 against Brown at the Yale Bowl (Yale Athletics' preview, Nov. 5, as indexed).

Last year, Nov. 8, 2025 at Brown Stadium — Yale 34, Brown 22. Josh Pitsenberger, since graduated, ran for 173 yards and opened the scoring with a 62-yard run on Yale's first play from scrimmage. Murphy threw for 366, Trevor Foley caught 6 for 145, and Crabtree kicked three field goals. Yale went on to win the Ivy title.

Brown scores: 2nd Drew Crabtree 29, 25 and 36 yd field goals (the last at the halftime gun); 3rd Matt Childs 5 yd run; 4th Ty Pezza 55 yd pass from James Murphy (2-pt failed).
Yale scores: 1st Josh Pitsenberger 62 yd run; 1st Nico Brown 12 yd pass from Dante Reno; 2nd Brown 21 yd pass from Reno; 3rd Pitsenberger 1 yd run; 4th Noah Piper 33 and 40 yd field goals.

Game day

The Yale Bowl

Opened Nov. 21, 1914, before more than 68,000 (Harvard won 36-0). The first bowl-shaped stadium in the country: the earth dug out for the field was banked into the stands. It inspired the Rose Bowl, the Los Angeles Coliseum and Michigan Stadium, and the Rose Bowl's name gave us every bowl game, the Super Bowl included. Capacity 61,446, the second largest in FCS. There are no locker rooms; players walk about 200 yards from the Smilow Field Center. A National Historic Landmark since 1987; FieldTurf since 2019 (Wikipedia).
